subject: general
question: When light travels from one medium to another medium then:

options.text: incident ray, normal at the point of incidence and refracted ray all are in the same plane
incident ray, normal at the point of incidence and reflected ray are in the same plane
incident ray, normal at the point of incidence and reflected ray are in two planes
incident ray, normal at the point of incidence and emerged ray, all are in the separate plane

solution:
The correct answer is __**incident ray, normal at the point of incidence and refracted ray all are in the same plane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When light travels from one medium to another medium, the incident ray, the normal at the point of incidence, and the refracted ray all lie in the same plane.
 
• This phenomenon is a part of the laws of refraction, specifically Snell's Law.
 
• The same principle applies to reflection, where the incident ray, the normal, and the reflected ray all lie in the same plane.
 
• The plane in which these rays lie is perpendicular to the surface at the point of incidence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Incident Ray:**

 
 
• The ray of light that strikes the surface is called the incident ray.
 
• It is the incoming ray which falls on the surface at a specific point.
 
 
 
• **Normal:**
 
 
• The normal is an imaginary line that is perpendicular to the surface at the point of incidence.
 
• It is used as a reference to measure the angles of incidence and refraction.
 
 
 
• **Refracted Ray:**
 
 
• The refracted ray is the ray that passes into the second medium and bends due to a change in speed.
 
• The angle between the refracted ray and the normal is called the angle of refraction.
 
 
 
• **Snell's Law:**
 
 
• Snell's Law relates the angles of incidence and refraction to the refractive indices of the two media.
